description: Build a deterministic feasible transportation allocation using Vogel's approximation method.

source.title: The Transportation Problem and the Vogel Approximation Method

output.encoding: total_cost*4^9 plus the fixed 3x3 row-major allocation matrix in nine base-4 digits

contract.penalty: For each active row or column, subtract its least active unit cost from its second least. A line with one active cell receives penalty 10, greater than every finite penalty in the cost domain.
contract.line_ties: Choose the maximum penalty. Scan active rows by increasing ID before active columns by increasing ID, replacing a selected line only for a strictly larger penalty; equal penalties retain the earlier row/column candidate.
contract.cell_ties: Within the chosen line, choose the cheapest active cell and then the lowest partner ID.
contract.allocation: Allocate the maximum feasible quantity min(remaining supply, remaining demand), update residual margins, and remove every exhausted row and column. Continue until all margins are zero.
contract.independent_method: The independent reference reconstructs each active row/column's candidate-cell list, sorts its costs to recompute the two-minimum penalty, selects with the documented stable ordering, and then verifies the resulting allocation encoding.
contract.invalid_cases: Null, malformed or trailing frames, out-of-range costs/margins, zero margins, or unequal total supply and demand return -1.
contract.distinction: VAM returns a feasible heuristic initial solution and does not guarantee minimum cost; it is distinct from exact min-cost flow and transportation simplex methods.

complexity.primary_time: O((R+C)*R*C) direct penalty scans over at most R+C-1 allocation iterations, with R,C<=3.
complexity.primary_space: O(R*C+R+C) for costs, allocations, and residual margins.
complexity.independent_time: O((R+C)*R*C*log(max(R,C))) due to independent per-line cost sorting, over at most R+C-1 iterations.
complexity.independent_space: O(R*C+R+C) for the direct matrix and active margins.
